text:
NextItNet’s original paper explicitly supports sampled softmax as an alternative to full-catalog softmax, making a loss-only experiment compatible with its causal convolution backbone. Recent evidence supports investigating objectives: [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates softmax using informative catalog subsets, reporting substantial memory savings while retaining recommendation quality. These results motivate testing multi-negative discrimination, but do not establish gains for this NextItNet benchmark. [Original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf).

Hardness needs restraint. [PSL (NeurIPS 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00163) identifies softmax’s sensitivity to false negatives and proposes alternative pairwise activations. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) identifies early hard-negative mining as a training failure risk; its approach starts with uniform sampling, then introduces global retrieval and curriculum-controlled hardness. Unobserved items are therefore uncertain negatives; excluding known training positives prevents obvious collisions without resolving latent relevance.

Practical hypothesis: first hold NextItNet architecture and depth aggregation fixed, replacing the baseline objective with cross-entropy over one positive plus multiple uniformly sampled negatives at each valid causal position. Suggested exploratory counts: 16 and 64; exclude padding, target collisions and known training positives. Then separately test a small fraction of negatives mined by the same network after uniform warm-up. These are proposed ablations, not published optimal settings. Preserve one trained checkpoint per category and select using the pinned macro validation HR@10; sampled training accuracy cannot establish held-out ranking gains. Combine with depth correction only after measuring the independent loss effect.
